original.statement: When cluster.inClusterEnabled is set to "false", Applications currently configured to sync on the in-cluster cluster will enter Unknown state and cannot sync; new Applications cannot use the in-cluster cluster; and deleting Applications will not delete their previously managed resources.

of.needed: which other Application destination settings (e.g. server URL) resolve to the in-cluster cluster

corrected.statement: Exposed: environments where cluster.inClusterEnabled is explicitly "false" AND some Application targets the in-cluster cluster. These Applications go to an Unknown state, cannot sync, and deleting them does not remove the resources they managed.

decision.reason: [ev-adf2ed32df1c] says the consequence only hits Applications "currently configured to sync on the in-cluster cluster" when `cluster.inClusterEnabled: "false"` is set. The proposed condition only checks the setting, so it also flags installs that have no in-cluster Applications, which makes it too broad. Its literal also wrongly includes the YAML quote marks: the configured value is the string false. Nothing in the evidence shows this is a Helm values path, so the corrected condition checks the config key in the ConfigMap data. The evidence names the "in-cluster" cluster but not how else an Application might target it, so that part is left undecidable.
